newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends down on Lujiazui fall.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends down on Lujiazui fall.

text.p: Shanghai B share index closed slightly down on Friday on heavy selling of real estate developer Lujiazui and trading was dominated by local investors, with foreigners absent due to Christmas, traders said.
The index edged down 0.116 points or 0.17 percent to 66.635 points, on volume of 20.3 million shares worth $10.3 million.

Brokers said local investors sold Lujiazui after the value of its existing shares had been diluted by a three-for-10 rights issue earlier this month. A total of 60 million new Lujiazui B shares from the rights issue were listed on Thursday.
Lujiazui traded the most on heavy liquidation selling, but some institutions were seen supporting it. It fell $0.030 or 2.25 percent to $1.302, on volume of 3.4 million shares.
But the market made up for most of its morning losses on cautious buying late in the session, mainly due to rises in the Shenzhen B share market, brokers said.
Shenzhen's B index closed at 142.33 points, up the daily limit of 10 percent or 12.95 points, and its A index closed at 332.30 points, up 6.39 percent or 19.97 points.
On the Shanghai market, 41 of 42 B shares traded, with 13 down, six flat and 22 up.

"In the past week, domestic investors dominated the market as overseas investors took their Christmas holiday," one broker said. "The market trend depends on the attitude of overseas investors after they come back next week."
"There will be more window-dressing buying of selective stocks next week with the approach of the year-end, but the index will meet resistance around 68 points," he said.
Hotel group New Asia was the biggest loser on expectations of poor results, falling $0.028 or 5.98 percent to $0.440, on volume of 410,600 shares.
Shanghai A share index dipped slightly on profit-taking and liquidation selling after rebounds in the past two days, with sentiment remaining cautious, brokers said.

The A index edged down 1.976 points or 0.21 percent to 960.902 points, on volume of 507.8 million shares worth 4.2 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index shed 15.389 points or 0.63 percent to 2445.612 points.
Fujian Yaohua was the biggest loser on institutional selling, falling 0.40 yuan or 4.70 percent to 8.10 yuan, on volume of 8.6 million shares.
